### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**5** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **178** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1028438748dfbb6a76a981a25310fe39c481fb2c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `85c63b5b2f987fe28711eb6a7e0926ed8a89f08f` — the merge of head `8ca7780c1a863d26cc9ca028d51be5aeb69514e9` into base `1028438748dfbb6a76a981a25310fe39c481fb2c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 85c63b5b2f987fe28711eb6a7e0926ed8a89f08f && git checkout 85c63b5b2f987fe28711eb6a7e0926ed8a89f08f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1028438748dfbb6a76a981a25310fe39c481fb2c 8ca7780c1a863d26cc9ca028d51be5aeb69514e9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1028438748dfbb6a76a981a25310fe39c481fb2c && git merge --no-ff 8ca7780c1a863d26cc9ca028d51be5aeb69514e9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1028438748dfbb6a76a981a25310fe39c481fb2c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8ca7780c1a863d26cc9ca028d51be5aeb69514e9`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts, packages/formula/src/validate.ts, packages/formula/src/validate.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-flow-condition-record-date-text.test.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/19.flow-condition-bare-ordering-before-record-date-arithmetic-refused.ts + read, not reviewed: packages/formula/src/index.ts and packages/formula/package.json (the package entry), packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.flow-condition-record-date-arithmetic-refused.ts, skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md, AGENTS.md (changeset rule); the changeset `.changeset/36377-flow-bare-ordering-record-date-arithmetic.md` read for ②

Inputs: card #36377 (body and its 4 comments: two triage notes, the claim 7210742031, the os-dev-report 7211625108; no earlier record or ruling on this card), PR #37840 body, file list (7 files) and net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on the head. Everything below marked "by code read" was traced in the tree at the head and not executed.

Check-runs on the head when read: none failed. Success: Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Type Check · source gates, Flag docs affected by code changes, Plan Test Core shards, Plan Test UI shards, Auto Label, filter. Skipped by their own conditions: 10 (opt-in harnesses, Build Docs, Queue verdict, Temporal Conformance and the like). STILL PENDING, so not judged here: Test Core 1/10 to 10/10, Build Core, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Lint · ESLint, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus. The new pins in this diff run in Test Core, so their gate verdict is not in yet; this record judges the design and the declaration, and landing still waits on those runs. The PR is a draft.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set, the declared change: RIGHT. In `typeSoundnessIssue` the record-root date-text pass is called only inside the `!mismatch` branch, and the #30025 swap can only replace a non-null `mismatch` with another non-null one, so `recordRootDateTextIssue` runs only where `firstTypeMismatch` answered null. The removed line stood down "because `firstTypeMismatch` answered", at the one place it had not. Traced for `due_date > "2026-01-01" && record.due_date + 1 > 5`: the bare pass meets `Timestamp > string`, `confirmAgainstDateText` returns null; the record-root pass in `firstTypeMismatch` meets the same ordering first, its date-text re-check faults on `DateText + int`, which is neither text nor boolean, so it returns null too; the bare date-text pass leaves the roots `dyn` and finds nothing. On `main` the roots-only typing then met `record.due_date + 1` and stood the last pass down: zero findings. At the head that pass answers `date-text-arithmetic-run-fails` (or `-run-may-fail`) naming the root read, which is what the all-root spelling already takes on `main` for the same reason (its own ordering comes first). Same code family, same arm rule (`dateArm('flattened', faultOutcome, false)`), same words.
- Accept-set, wider than the declared sentence: RIGHT in behaviour, under-described in words (N1 below). The removed stand-down was not specific to an ordering against a text literal. By code read, every flattened condition where a bare-name shape makes `firstTypeMismatch` answer null ahead of root date arithmetic is newly refused with the same code: a concatenation first (`"Due: " + due_date != "" && record.due_date + 1 > 5`, `string + Timestamp` confirmed away), a bare date ordered against a number first (`due_date > 5 && record.due_date + 1 > 5`, `Timestamp > int` is neither date arithmetic nor a text/boolean mismatch, so null). In each, the root arithmetic is real and faults whenever it is evaluated, so none is a false refusal.
- No false refusal found. The pass types every bare name `dyn` and the roots as the date text, keeps only `date-text-call*` / `date-text-arithmetic*`, and a root member is never shadowed by a flow variable, so a finding needs arithmetic (or a call) on a date field's text through `record.` / `previous.`, which the evaluator cannot answer. The clean controls are pinned at all three levels (`... && record.due_date > today()`-style ordering, `daysBetween`, `addDays`).
- The flow-variable case (`flowVariables: ['due_date']`) answering `date-arithmetic-run-fails`: RIGHT and unchanged by this diff. With the bare name shadowed there is no bare ordering fault, so `firstTypeMismatch`'s own record-root pass answers, as for `record.due_date + 1 > 5` alone.
- Public surface: RIGHT. `recordRootReadsFaultDateArith` was `export`ed from `cel-engine.ts` but `packages/formula/src/index.ts` never re-exported it and `package.json` exports only `.`; its single caller is the removed line. No published symbol moves. No schema, no error code and no message text is added: every code the mixed spelling can now take already exists on `main`.
- Run-time behaviour: unchanged (no evaluator hunk). `registerFlow` stays advisory per the changeset and the entry; not re-verified here beyond the absence of any hunk in that path.
- Pins: the formula test asserts the mixed spelling's verdict deep-equals the all-root spelling's and that the evaluator faults on it; lint asserts it at start, edge and decision; runtime asserts the publish door (INVALID_METADATA, 422, draft kept) and a publishing control. The ablation the PR body reports (2 red on re-inserting the stand-down) is the dev's account and was not re-run.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — present line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset, with `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. Correct on both counts: no schema or governed path is in the tree, and a value an author could publish is now refused.

The changeset sets `@objectstack/formula` and `@objectstack/spec` to `minor`. That matches the rule (a `narrowed` kind takes at least `minor` on each package the diff moves): formula carries the source change, spec gains a migration entry; lint and runtime change only test files and publish nothing new. It carries the BREAKING banner, a FROM → TO table, the `adr-0087: registered flow-condition-bare-ordering-before-record-date-arithmetic-refused` line, and the entry with that exact id exists in the diff as a structured TODO (no mechanical rewrite is possible, as for entry 18). The title carries `!`. `Check Changeset` concluded success. Level and declarations match what the diff publishes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the os-dev-report. Nothing to answer.
- Dev flag, route replaced (the verdict family is `date-text-arithmetic`, not the dispatch's `date-arithmetic`): ACCEPTED. It is the card's own second fix direction, and it is the only choice that gives the mixed spelling the verdict its all-root spelling has on `main`; answering `date-arithmetic` would have made two spellings of one fault disagree.
- Dev flag, card nits: N3 is pinned (the #30025 swap returning a root `date-arithmetic` verdict). N1 and N2 are "noted, not filed" with `carrier: none`, while the card's done-when reads "nits pinned or split off". Recorded as N3 below; the lane seat either files the follow-up or accepts the deviation by name. Both are best-effort naming / arm choices on an expression that is refused either way.
- Dev flag, runtime `check:test-typecheck` naming three test files the diff does not touch: not answerable from here; `Type Check · workspace` is pending and is the verdict. `Type Check · source gates` is green.
- File surface: the claim named `packages/formula/src/**` plus pins and the changeset. The spec migration entry sits outside that wording, but ADR-0087 requires it for a breaking changeset and #36333 set the pattern; the lint and runtime files are pins. No breach worth escalating.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): not applicable. The diff is a type-check pass over an expression string; it adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.
- Escalated: nothing.

### ④ Design judgment

Does the narrowing take a declared capability away, or make the spec's own refusal real? The second. Nothing published on `main` declares arithmetic against a number on a date field's text as something a flow condition can do: `skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md` states the build refuses `date + n` with no site or spelling excepted, semantic entry 18 on `main` already refuses `record.FIELD + n` / `previous.FIELD - n` in flow conditions, and the all-bare and all-root spellings of this very condition are refused on `main`. The mixed spelling passed only through an ordering accident between two passes, and the capability it would need (the evaluator adding a number to a `YYYY-MM-DD` text) does not exist and is not promised anywhere. So this is not a consumer-side narrowing of a declared capability, and "implement or retire" does not apply.

Attempts to break it, all by code read:
- A condition newly refused that runs fine: none found (see ①). A guard cannot rescue the arithmetic either, and the guarded forms are refused in the all-root spelling already, so the two stay consistent.
- A condition of the card's shape still accepted: none found for arithmetic that has the root read as an operand.
- A neighbouring shape still accepted (outside this card, see N4).
- Removing the stand-down instead of repairing it: sound. Its premise can never hold at its only call site, so a repaired version would be dead code.
- Docblocks in `validate.ts` and `cel-engine.ts` now describe the order as the code has it.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Nits (none moves the verdict; a fix belongs on the prose faces only, or in a follow-up card, since any other fix moves the head and this record stops covering it):
- N1 (nit, declaration wording): the entry's `surface` and the changeset's first sentences name one precedent, a bare date ordered against a text literal. The mechanism is general (① second bullet). The changeset's one-line fix already says "whatever precedes it", which is the true extent; the PR body and changeset prose could say so once. The entry's `surface` is not a prose face: leave it as an accepted deviation.
- N2 (nit, prose): "failed on every run" overstates it. `&&` stops at a false left side, so a row whose `due_date` is not after the literal evaluates to false without reaching the arithmetic; the flow fails on every run where the ordering holds. The same is true of the all-bare and all-root spellings and of the existing `run-fails` wording, so this is the family's convention, not this PR's error. By CEL semantics, not measured.
- N3 (nit, card done-when): card nits N1 and N2 are neither pinned nor split off (③). Follow-up card or a named acceptance.
- N4 (nit, outside the diff, follow-up candidate): the same masking survives where the later arithmetic has no date-field operand. By code read, `due_date > "2026-01-01" && today() + 30 > record.due_date` (and the bare-only `due_date > "2026-01-01" && today() + 30 > today()`) is accepted at the head as on `main`: the bare ordering stands `firstTypeMismatch` down, and the date-text passes only report a fault with a date text as an operand, which `Timestamp + int` is not. `today() + 30` is refused when written first. Pre-existing, not introduced here, and not the card's shape (no arithmetic on a root read), so it is a candidate card, to be measured first.
